_note: Global 10R leadership layer. Leader labels, summaries and every advisor line are Will's, verbatim from GS10R_SPEC_leadership-succession-content-layer_2026-09-20.md (sections 4-6). Dispositions encode his own 'arises from' column; succession pools are derived from the same column and want his confirmation. Leaders carry no tuning bends: Will made no directional tuning claim per archetype, and this build does not invent one. Ladders name no Enduring Issue out loud - supplying the word is the student's job.

unrest._note: Measured against real engine runs on 2026-09-20, not balanced: a town taxed to the ceiling and never policed sits in the high 50s to low 70s for years, a well-run one peaks near 2. A balance pass owns the final numbers (scope doc stage 4).

leaders.label: The Founding Council
leaders.summary: The council that answered, at the town's founding, the question every government has to answer: what makes power legitimate?

leaders.label: The Heir
leaders.summary: Power passed the way it was always going to — by blood, not by testing.

leaders.label: The Reformer
leaders.summary: Chosen because the old answer to 'how much control is too much' had stopped working, and someone offered a new one before it broke.

leaders.label: The Strongman
leaders.summary: Order restored, at a price the town is still paying.

leaders.label: The Revolutionary Council
leaders.summary: The people's own government, replacing the one that stopped being theirs.

tiers: The people grumble, but they still line up for bread, my lord.
They're starting to ask whether obedience was ever the same as consent.
This is what every government built on that bargain has looked like, right before it broke.
The watch is heavier on the streets than it used to be, mayor.
Folks are asking who the guards are actually protecting.
This is what it looks like right before people stop calling it order and start calling it something else.
ladders._source: Will spec section 5, Human Rights ladder

tiers: Taxes are the talk of the tavern this week, mayor.
They're asking who the burden actually falls on.
This is what it looks like right before people decide the cost isn't worth the bargain anymore.
There's a flag flying in the square that isn't yours, my lord.
They're not asking you for anything anymore. They're asking each other.
This is what it looks like right before a people stop asking to be governed and start governing themselves.
